Strategy Consultancies

High-level board mandates, enterprise AI strategy, organizational transformation, and operating-model design.

Global Systems Integrators
(GSIs) & Big 4

Full-scale multi-cloud architecture, large enterprise deployments, operational workflows, systems integration, and AI governance/compliance.

Accenture, IBM Consulting, Capgemini, TCS, Infosys, Deloitte, PwC, EY.

Specialized AI Boutiques
& Pure-Play Agencies

Deep machine learning engineering, rapid custom prototyping, vertical algorithmic design, and "Decision as a Service" models.

Fractal Analytics, LatentView Analytics, Slalom, Cambridge Consultants, Silo AI, Alice Labs.

2. Market Sizing, Estimated AI Service Revenue & Market Share Indicators

MBB / Strategy Consultancies:

Revenue Footprint: BCG attributes ~20% of its $13.5B total revenue (~$2.7B) to AI advisory. McKinsey projects ~40% of its future business will be directly AI-driven.

Market Share / Deal Economics: High-margin engagements typically ranging from $2M to $20M+, leveraging the "10-20-70" rule (10% algorithms, 20% technology, 70% people/process change).

GSIs & Big 4:

Revenue Footprint: Accenture leads with $5.9B in new GenAI bookings (FY25) and $2.7B in advanced AI revenues. IBM Consulting has accumulated a $6B AI book of business.

Market Share / Deal Economics: Commands the largest overall volume of enterprise AI spend via large multi-year T&M and outcome-based system-integration contracts, notably across regulated sectors.

Specialized AI Boutiques:

Revenue Footprint: Fractal Analytics reached a $1.3B valuation with >$381M LTM revenue. LatentView Analytics exceeded $125M (₹1,060 Cr) in operational revenue.

Market Share / Deal Economics: Focuses on mid-market deployments and specialized departmental projects, capturing deals within the $50K–$400K range or at specialized rates of $100–$300/hour.

3. Dedicated AI Units & Key M&A Activity

Strategy Consultancies:

  • QuantumBlack (McKinsey): Over 1,700 technical specialists across 40+ offices; acquired MLOps platform Iguazio to accelerate deployment workflows.
  • BCG X (BCG): Proprietary tech and venture build arm with an exclusive strategic deployment partnership with Anthropic.
  • Vector (Bain): Global digital/data delivery team backed by an enterprise co-innovation partnership with OpenAI.

GSIs & Big 4:

  • Accenture Center for Advanced AI: Core anchor of Accenture's $3B AI investment, supported by an 80,000+ data and AI practitioner network driving the AI Refinery framework.
  • Deloitte, PwC & EY: Deloitte operates a 40,000+ specialist practice leading Claude enterprise rollouts; PwC deployed a $1B GenAI investment; EY targets sovereign AI advisory.
  • Capgemini: Acquired BPO and digital transformation leader WNS to accelerate end-to-end AI process integration.

Specialized Boutiques:

  • Fractal: Developed internal venture models, spinning off AI platforms such as Cogentiq (agentic workflows) and Qure.ai (healthcare).
  • LatentView Analytics: Acquired Decision Point to build dedicated Revenue Growth Management (RGM) capabilities.
  • Silo AI: Acquired by AMD to build an integrated full-stack hardware/software AI ecosystem.
[KEY FINDINGS] The market is structurally split between high-margin organizational transformation (MBB), high-volume systems integration and governance (Big 4/GSIs), and niche algorithmic engineering (AI Boutiques). /// Enterprise AI service revenues have surged rapidly, highlighted by Accenture's $5.9B GenAI bookings, IBM's $6B AI pipeline, and BCG generating ~$2.7B (20% of firm revenue) from AI. /// Major strategy firms align tightly with foundation model providers (e.g., Bain-OpenAI, BCG-Anthropic), while scaling their dedicated technical units (QuantumBlack, BCG X). /// M&A activity focuses on acquiring proprietary engineering assets and MLOps tooling (e.g., McKinsey acquiring Iguazio, AMD acquiring Silo AI, LatentView acquiring Decision Point).
